cards.front: Transformer (Vaswani et al. 2017) scaled dot-product attention (formula)
cards.why: Each query is compared with every key by a dot product; the softmax turns the scores into weights over the values. \(Q, K, V\): query, key and value matrices; \(d_k\): key dimension.

cards.front: Transformer attention: reason for dividing by \(\sqrt{d_k}\)
cards.back: Large dot products push the softmax into regions with tiny gradients
cards.why: For components with unit variance, \(q \cdot k\) has variance \(d_k\); dividing by \(\sqrt{d_k}\) brings it back to 1 whatever the key dimension.

cards.back: Low-rank \(B A\) added to the frozen weights: \(W_0 + BA\)
cards.why: \(B \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times r}\), \(A \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times k}\) with rank \(r \ll \min(d, k)\), so far fewer parameters are trained, and \(BA\) can be merged into \(W_0\) for inference at no extra cost.

cards.title: Transformer encoder layer: sublayers (in data-flow order)
cards.remarks: The original paper normalises after each residual addition (post-norm); many later models normalise before (pre-norm), which trains more stably.
